items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: He wanted to use a classical term that’s called motor rhythms, which Stravinsky used all the time.

ctx.x: The computer doesn’t need to breathe.

I’m just going through this with a saxophone player who is very talented and a very talented writer, he’s going to be incredible. And he came in with a shout chorus. He’s got trumpets starting on a high B above the staff. There’s written notes, D, E, F. And he wanted to use a classical term that’s called motor rhythms, which Stravinsky used all the time. He’d get this one thing going, like [humms] from “Firebird,” and underneath it, [humms]. And he’s got these two different things happening [humms], and it’s like…
